difficulty_reason: The argument constructs a synchronized product automaton for arbitrary integer moments and explicitly classifies its reachable states to obtain primitive Perron-Frobenius growth. It then controls the inaccessible spectral blocks and reduces arbitrary binary matrix products to two-dimensional factors with sharp spectral-norm bounds. These local constructions identify the generalized spectral radius, allowing a Kronecker-power limit theorem to determine the asymptotic moment exponent.

source_check.note: One combined unit preserves shared moment automaton and its spectral-radius construction; no separate counting of exponents, spectral-radius helper or parameter values. Power sums are comparable up to p-dependent constants, not a full asymptotic equivalent for all integer N. Counts distinct strictly increasing Fibonacci terms with f1=1,f2=2; positive integer p. Berstel automaton, Zeckendorf uniqueness, Perron-Frobenius automaton theorem, Blondel–Nesterov nonnegative Kronecker-power limit and Berger–Wang equality are named prerequisites. All new reachable-state classification, inaccessible triangular blocks and binary-product spectral control is printed. Finite transition checks (t1–t10) are bounded checks from the displayed four-state automaton; spectral-norm values h=2–7 are explicitly bounded finite2×2 matrix checks. No omitted new core.
